headline: Chinese Fire Ant burrows into Cisco routers to steal credentials and erase logs as PaperCut zero-days land on CISA's must-patch list and attackers weaponize AI to both dodge malware analysis and hunt exposed credentials.

emerging_trends.text: Attackers now treat AI as both weapon and cover—UAC-0099 buried a GuardBreaker prompt in a malicious script to derail Ukraine's AI-assisted malware analysis, while other crews impersonate ClaudeBot and rival AI crawlers to scan for exposed credentials.

China-nexus Fire Ant has moved off VMware hypervisors and onto Cisco IOS XR routers and TACACS servers, showing how nation-state crews increasingly nest in the network gear that authenticates and routes high-value traffic.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Fire Ant Hijacks Cisco Routers for Espionage

emerging_trends.text: Active exploitation keeps driving the patch calendar, with PaperCut's print-server zero-days now carrying remote access tools and landing on CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog under a federal patch deadline.
emerging_trends.topic_title: PaperCut Zero-Days Draw Remote Access Tools and KEV Listing

topics.title: Berlin Refuses Rhysida Ransom Demand
topics.latest_developments: Berlin confirmed data theft and tied the mid-August breach to the Rhysida ransomware gang, which listed the city on its leak site and claims over 5TB including personal information and credentials; Governing Mayor Kai Wegner said the city will not pay.
topics.summary: Rhysida, a ransomware and extortion group, breached Berlin's city administration in mid-August 2026 and now demands payment. Wegner refuses and warns residents of exposed personal data.

sources.title: Berlin says it won't pay ransom after hackers steal government data
Berlin confirms data theft after Rhysida ransomware attack claims
Berlin Won't Pay Extortion Group Claiming Data Theft

topics.title: PaperCut Zero-Days Draw Remote Access Tools and KEV Listing
topics.latest_developments: PaperCut Software reported that the threat actor now covertly installs legitimate remote access software on compromised servers, and CISA added CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
topics.summary: PaperCut warned on August 27, 2026 of in-the-wild attacks on internet-facing NG and MF print servers, where unauthenticated attackers run code; CISA's Binding Operational Directive 26-04 orders federal agencies to patch. Administrators should restrict web access and update immediately.

sources.title: Attackers plant remote access tools on compromised PaperCut servers
CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog

topics.title: Fire Ant Hijacks Cisco Routers for Espionage
topics.latest_developments: Sygnia found China-nexus Fire Ant expanding beyond VMware hypervisors to compromise Cisco IOS XR routers, TACACS servers, and Linux management hosts, planting an unexplained GRE tunnel to intercept traffic, steal credentials, and blind security logs.
topics.summary: Fire Ant, a China-nexus espionage actor, targets the core network gear that routes, authenticates, and manages high-value networks. Operators running Cisco IOS XR and TACACS should hunt for GRE tunnels absent from running configuration or commit history.

sources.title: Chinese Fire Ant hackers turn Cisco routers into spying platforms
China-Linked Fire Ant Hijacks Cisco Routers to Steal Credentials and Blind Security Logs

topics.title: Hackers Poison AI Malware Analysis
topics.latest_developments: ESET found Russia-aligned UAC-0099 embedding a nuclear-weapon prompt—which ESET named GuardBreaker—as comments in a malicious VBS script to trip AI safety filters and derail AI-assisted malware analysis in Ukraine, and separately someone hid AI instructions inside a court filing.
topics.summary: Prompt injection lets attackers steer AI tools with hidden instructions. UAC-0099 feeds Ukrainian analysts' AI a manipulative comment, and a litigant slipped commands into a legal filing; defenders should treat every model input as untrusted.

sources.title: Russian hackers plant nuclear weapon prompt in malware to trip AI safety guardrails
Hiding Prompt Injection in Legal Filing

topics.title: Spring Ring Voice Phishing Hits Microsoft Teams
topics.latest_developments: Unit 42 detailed Spring Ring, a campaign whose callers abuse Microsoft Teams and voice phishing to talk victims into running malware and then push toward enterprise domain controllers.
topics.summary: Spring Ring operators pose as support staff over Microsoft Teams to deploy malware and reach domain controllers. Enterprises should restrict external Teams messaging and voice calls and train staff against help-desk impersonation.

sources.title: Spring Ring: An Inside Look at Voice Phishing Campaigns in Microsoft Teams

topics.title: Attackers Pose as AI Crawlers to Hunt Credentials
topics.latest_developments: GreyNoise reported attackers copying the user-agent strings that AI crawlers announce—Anthropic's ClaudeBot and the crawlers of OpenAI, Google, and Perplexity—to disguise credential-hunting scans as legitimate bot traffic.
topics.summary: Every visitor names itself in one request line, and attackers now spoof AI crawler headers to blend in while scanning sites for exposed credentials and configuration files. Site owners should verify crawler identity by source network rather than the header alone.

sources.title: Threat actors are posing as AI crawlers to hunt for exposed credentials
